nodes.label: PeopleStep component (confirm people, QR code)
nodes.rationale: Runs the person long-poll only in the 'people' phase and the group long-poll only in the 'group' phase, so the page never has two requests waiting on the bot at once; offers 'Stop the background service' when Telegram answers a 409 conflict.

nodes.label: useLongPoll hook
nodes.rationale: Repeatedly calls the server (each call waits up to 25s server-side on Telegram) until it finds something, turning 'quiet' after hintAfterMs; a found value stays pending on the server, so React StrictMode's duplicate effect or an unmount-abandoned request loses nothing.

nodes.label: LogsPage component (self-polling log viewer)
nodes.rationale: Asks /api/manage/logs again intervalMs (default 2s) after each answer, with the chosen level/event filter, only while the page is mounted; the polling loop self-schedules its own setTimeout rather than using a fixed interval, and stops cleanly on unmount.

nodes.label: usePath hook (path + navigate)
nodes.rationale: Ruling 5: no router dependency. usePath() is built directly over window.location.pathname, history.pushState and the popstate event, since UiServer already answers index.html for every extensionless page path (/, /projects, /people, /settings, /logs).

nodes.label: dispatch.ui.ApiException
nodes.rationale: Lets an API route answer with its own HTTP status and error code (e.g. 409 conflict when another process already reads the bot's Telegram updates), distinct from the generic 400-for-CliException/500-for-anything-else handling UiServer already had.

nodes.label: dispatch.ui.Folders (folder browser listing)
nodes.rationale: Lists only directory names on the machine running Dispatch and whether each is a git clone; it never returns file contents, satisfying the security constraint that only folder names (not content) cross to the browser, and caps listings at 500 entries (MAX_ENTRIES) marking truncation.

nodes.label: ServiceCommand.specFor / runningJar
nodes.rationale: Splits the background service's Service.Spec construction out of ServiceCommand.install into a public static specFor, so the web UI's SetupApi can install the service without a terminal front end.

nodes.label: dispatch.ui.SetupApi (setup's HTTP steps)
nodes.rationale: Exposes dispatch init's steps as POST routes, keeping answers in memory until Write (nothing written before). people/next and group/next long-poll Telegram up to 25s; a found candidate stays pending on the server so a request the browser abandoned (e.g. React StrictMode's second effect) never loses anyone. Telegram is read one request at a time via a 'reading' lock.

nodes.label: UiServer (POST routes with JSON bodies)
nodes.rationale: Adds POST route support (JSON body up to 64 KiB, malformed JSON -> 400, oversized -> 413, unknown path -> 404, wrong method -> 405) so setup and management can be driven by POST calls; every non-GET request already needed the page's Origin header.

nodes.label: dispatch.config.ConfigEdit (in-place YAML edits)
nodes.rationale: Ruling 1: saving edits the YAML text in place using SnakeYAML node marks (set/remove/append) so only changed lines change, preserving comments, order and spacing; the file is replaced only through ConfigFile.replace (validate, then atomic move). This supersedes the original spec's 'rewrite the whole file' approach and its warning that comments will be lost. A flow-style collection ({...} or [...]) is refused with a message rather than edited, since editing inside one in place is error-prone.

nodes.label: dispatch.ui.ManageApi (management reads/saves, logs, restart)
nodes.rationale: Every management read answers 'version': the config file's SHA-256; every save sends it back, and a mismatch answers 409 changed ('the config changed on disk since this page loaded it; reload to see the change') - stale-edit detection is stateless, keyed purely on the file hash. Each save keeps dispatch.yaml.bak (the previous exact bytes, with the config's own POSIX permissions) written just before the validated ConfigFile.replace, so an aborted validation still leaves a harmless backup equal to the unchanged file. Unchanged values are never rewritten (e.g. 60m stays 60m although the page shows it as 1h). Removing a member also drops them from telegram.admins when no longer in any group, refused if it would leave no admin or leave a group empty; removing a project is refused if it is the last project or the only project of its group. Reading the service log uses a 'ponytail: only the log's last 1 MiB is read' shortcut (TAIL_BYTES), so a narrow filter can find fewer lines than asked; the stated upgrade path is reading further back in chunks if that matters. Restart (/api/service/restart) is refused with 400 when no service is installed.

nodes.label: Playwright end-to-end suite (ui/e2e/*) against the real dispatch ui jar
nodes.norm_label: playwright end-to-end suite (ui/e2e/*) against the real dispatch ui jar
nodes.rationale: The only new dependency (@playwright/test, dev-only, never bundled into the jar) permitted for UI-3a, because the spec requires real browser end-to-end tests and nothing already installed drives a real browser. nodes.label: Service.restart() default method
nodes.rationale: Ruling 4: default implementation is stop() then start(); a service manager with a native one-step restart (systemd) overrides it. launchd and Task Scheduler restart by stop-then-start too (bootout+bootstrap, /End+/Run), since only systemd has a genuine one-step restart worth overriding.
